assessment.forecast_review_en: The previous forecast was partially confirmed, as the main focus in markets is indeed shifting towards preparations and expectations surrounding upcoming US-China summits.

articles.summary:
Hong Kong police suspect a dog attack may have caused the death of a woman who was taken to hospital in the early hours of Sunday, the South China Morning Post has learned.
A force spokesman said the woman was found unconscious beside a bicycle on Pok Wai South Road at 12.42am.

articles.summary:
Hong Kong prosecutors are set to open the murder trial of three former relatives of slain socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung later this week, three years after her killing shocked the city and drew international attention.

articles.summary:
Hong Kong’s first five-year plan will give businesses greater certainty to make long-term investment decisions amid a volatile external environment, the city’s finance chief has said.

Chinese firms have shown “very strong interest” in investing in Oman – across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran – as they aim to tap the lucrative Middle East market while minimising risks, an Omani official said.

articles.title: The cooling trap: how Asia’s air conditioners are making heatwaves worse
articles.summary:
As heatwaves become more frequent and intense across Asia, the region faces a dangerous power paradox. Soaring demand for air conditioning threatens to push electricity grids closer to failure just as extreme heat puts the infrastructure under greater strain, raising the risk of cooling disappearing when people need it most.
That risk has been visible across the region this summer.

articles.summary:
A man in eastern China filed a lawsuit against an AI company after he followed a chatbot’s recommendation for his mother’s burial date, which he later claimed was linked to a family misfortune.
According to Jimu News, Shi, from Jiashan county in Zhejiang province, lost his mother to a sudden illness in April.

articles.summary:
Zhang Dongdong has been fielding ever more requests for legal advice from jittery entrepreneurs, nervous government officials or their desperate relatives.
They usually do not tell him the whole story, and sometimes say it happened “to a friend”, but most want to know the same thing: what to do when they are targeted by China’s corruption busters.

articles.summary:
In late August, I took my parents to see Once Upon a Time in the Middle East in their small-town cinema on the mainland. Built around an unnamed conflict widely understood to be the US-led Iraq war, the film has become the kind of phenomenon no marketing budget could buy, projected to reach 2.5 billion yuan (US$372.5 million) largely through word of mouth.

articles.title: Xi sends condolences as Hong Kong holds state funeral for Tung Chee-hwa – as it happened
articles.summary:
Hong Kong bid farewell to its first post-colonial chief executive, Tung Chee-hwa, at a state funeral on Sunday – only the third time a Hongkonger has received such an honour since the 1997 handover.
Tung, who died at the age of 89 on September 8, led Hong Kong through a series of ups and downs, including the 1997 Asian financial crisis, the 2003 Sars outbreak and the V-shaped economic recovery that followed.
